title: Long range spatial correlations in the periodically driven transverse field Ising model
abstract: We consider a periodically driven transverse field Ising model and study the long-time behavior of the correlations between the excitations in the spin chain. We show that the longest correlation length is defined by the interference between the topological defects induced by the analog of the Kibble-Zurek mechanism and those induced by the Floquet resonance. We show that although the correlations always have a finite correlation length since the system is integrable, the correlation length can be made arbitrarily large by tuning the drive period.
summary: This paper investigates spatial correlations in a periodically driven transverse field Ising model. By analyzing the pole structure of the correlation function, the authors show that tuning the drive period allows for constructive interference between different excitation sources (Kibble-Zurek and Floquet resonances). This interference leads to an unusually slow, algebraic decay of correlations, suggesting control over quantum coherence in driven many-body systems.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the long-time spatial correlations of excitations within a periodically driven transverse field Ising model.
main_result: The correlation length can be made arbitrarily large by tuning the drive period, due to constructive interference between contributions from the Kibble-Zurek mechanism and Floquet resonances, leading to an optimal algebraic decay rate of r^-2.
method: The analysis uses Jordan-Wigner transformations to map spins to fermions, followed by analyzing the pole structure of the correlation function in momentum space near the unit circle.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional Transverse Field Ising Model (TFIM) subjected to a periodic drive $g(t)$. The Hamiltonian involves nearest-neighbor interactions and a time-dependent transverse field term.
key_observables: Longest correlation length ($\xi$) and the spatial correlation function $ho(r, t)$ for excitations.
important_parameters: The driving period ($T$), which must satisfy specific conditions related to Floquet resonances; the coupling constants $g_0$ and $g_1$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on identifying poles in the correlation function integral, specifically requiring the interference between two distinct pole contributions.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates numerical calculations of $|ho(r)|$ for varying drive amplitudes. Figure 3 compares the analytically derived optimal envelope $|ho^*(r)|$ with its calculated form at specific resonance conditions.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the system's dynamics by transforming it into a fermionic problem, deriving the correlation function from four-fermion expectation values, and then performing a detailed pole analysis to identify the mechanism responsible for long-range correlations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium dynamics in periodically driven quantum systems, which is highly relevant to understanding Floquet engineering and how external driving can manipulate correlation decay rates beyond equilibrium predictions.
